commits.messageBody:
A Claude Max account that has used up its weekly Fable allowance goes on
serving Opus, Sonnet and Haiku, and answers a Fable request with "You've
reached your Fable limit. Switch to another model, or manage usage credits at
claude.ai/settings/usage?from=cc_cli_limit_message, to continue." That is the
headless wording of CLI 2.1.284 and 2.1.289 for an account that can buy
credits, and classifyError did not know the suffix: the refusal was an
api_error, a 500, and priority routing failed nothing over. On a working
proxy 57 Fable requests in seven minutes came back that way while another
profile in the pool had allowance left.

classifyError accepts the suffix now, with either of the two addresses the
CLI's refusal builder puts in it, for the tier banner and for "You're out of
usage credits", whose pattern also stopped at the end of the message and so
never matched once the subprocess's stderr was appended.

Recognising the refusal is half of it. A quota refusal benched the whole
account, and this account is not out: for ten minutes at a time every
conversation it held would have moved to another account, and back when the
bench ran out, each move rewriting that conversation's prompt cache. So a
refusal has a scope. limitModelScope confines it to the refused request's
model when the window Anthropic named is that model's own: seven_day_fable
from the wording, which parseLimitWording now reads, or the SDK's
seven_day_overage_included on a Fable request, which is what the refused
request's rate_limit_event carried. An account out of usage credits is out
for the models billed to them and no others. ProfileExhaustion keeps such a
mark apart from the account-wide ones and a request is kept away by an
account-wide mark or by its own model's; a request that names no model the
proxy knows goes by the tier it is run as.

The scope is decided on what the refused attempt itself was told. An SDK
event is read for fifteen minutes, so one from an earlier request does not
confine a refusal, and neither does the event of a request that was served
past its allowance on usage credits, which the CLI also reports as rejected.
In both cases, as for a window that was guessed or belongs to another model,
the account is benched as before.

The mark lasts until the reset the SDK gave with the refusal. A refusal known
only by its wording has none of its own: it takes the reset of that model's
window from the last usage read when the read shows the window spent, ten
minutes otherwise, and the forced read that follows extends it on the same
condition. An account out of usage credits is asked again every ten minutes,
credits coming back when they are bought.

When every account refuses, Retry-After is the wait until the first account
in the pool can serve that model again. It was the wait for the accounts
tried on the request, and with everything benched only the active one is
tried: its allowance was five days off, an account behind it reopened in four
minutes, and the client was told to wait a day. The retry_after in the body
says the same, which is the only wait a streamed refusal carries; it was the
last attempt's own.

GET /profiles/health lists accounts out for one model under exhaustedModels.
exhausted, there and on /profiles/list, is unchanged: the accounts that are
out altogether.

scripts/e2e-model-allowance-failover-live.mjs holds it against real
profiles, one with the allowance spent: a streamed request and one that is
not are refused by the active account and served by the next, the active
account is out for fable until its reset and not out altogether, Haiku is
still served by it, and the next Fable request is tried on the second account
only. With a second spent account in its place every account refuses, and
the wait is the pool's in the header, the body and the stream's frame. The
running build answered the first of those requests with a 500. E2E.md E78 has
the runs, the review the second half of this came out of, and what is not
covered, the builder's two other headless banners among it.

(cherry picked from commit 9cc451c435cea66ffaf3d2ee30bc77a69a23b4bf)
commits.messageHeadline: fix: fail over a model whose allowance is spent, and only that model

commits.messageBody:
A Fable refusal that arrives behind a keepalive ping is decided inside the
client's stream, after headers are out; it must still leave only a Fable
mark and keep other models on the account. Forgetting a profile drops its
per-model marks along with the account-wide one.
commits.messageHeadline: test(routing): cover model-scoped benches on the in-stream failover path

commits.messageBody:
resolvePriorityOrder appends every configured profile, and resolveProfile
only returns a configured one, so the active profile is always in the order.
The branch that prepended it to the wait's pool could never run.
commits.messageHeadline: refactor(routing): take the pool wait from the resolved priority order

commits.messageBody:
- A refusal on record that predates the attempt benches the account whole.
- An active account skipped as benched still counts toward the pool wait.
- A turn held to its retained account is told that account's own wait.
commits.messageHeadline: test(routing): hold the allowance freshness check and both pool waits

commits.messageBody:
The JSON answer carries it for a retryable status; a refusal inside the
stream carries it only for a quota refusal; a retained turn waits for its own
account. E2E.md counts the new mocked cases and the mutations they catch.
commits.messageHeadline: docs(profiles): say which exhausted-pool refusals carry the pool wait

commits.messageBody:
Read effective account and requested-model exclusions when the pool refusal is returned, rather than retaining shorter attempted marks. Keep the retained-account pool boundary and the default retry wait when an eligible bench has already expired.

Cover repeated shorter marks, overlapping exclusions, skipped accounts, asynchronous refinement, expiry, retained continuations and ordinary first refusals through mocked HTTP JSON and SSE.
commits.messageHeadline: fix: derive pool retry waits from effective benches
